claims.statement: `read_file` routes backend-declared base64 content to multimodal ToolMessage blocks rather than line-numbered text, choosing a block type from the extension when known and retaining the validated source path and MIME type in message metadata.

`UnsupportedContentMiddleware` runs on each model request and replaces only multimodal blocks the active model explicitly cannot accept with a read-file-path placeholder, without mutating persisted messages; `create_deep_agent` adds it after its core, memory, and HITL middleware before subsequent stack shaping.

FilesystemMiddleware orders synthetic media messages emitted by read_file after the complete ToolMessage batch, and on a ModelInvalidRequestError retries after replacing only latest-turn multimodal read_file content; unrelated invalid model requests still raise.

FilesystemMiddleware requires an initialized backend rather than a backend factory, chooses a state schema with a `files` channel when any composite branch is state-backed, and rejects binary offload when its blob path routes to StateBackend.

A `ReadResult` validates coherent pagination metadata, while backend reads must tolerate negative offsets and non-positive limits; text formatting remains middleware responsibility rather than backend responsibility.
FilesystemMiddleware filters `delete` and `execute` from a model request when the active backend does not support those optional capabilities, even if they were allowed at construction.

Generic large-message handling offloads oversized human messages and tool text to backend artifact paths with previews, but filesystem tools are excluded from generic result eviction because their results are already bounded or compact.

With `offload_binary_content=True`, FilesystemMiddleware offloads binary payloads only from `read_file` results and eligible human media to SHA-256-addressed backend blob files, persists references instead of base64 payloads, and rehydrates verified payloads for model requests.
Binary blob offload is best effort: upload errors retain inline payloads, and malformed, unavailable, or digest-mismatched blob references are replaced by a text notice rather than rehydrated.
FilesystemMiddleware rejects parallel write, edit, or delete calls in one model response when their canonicalized paths are the same, preventing competing mutations of one logical file.

`FilesystemMiddleware` exposes the built-in `ls`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `delete`, `glob`, `grep`, and `execute` tools according to its model-facing allowlist; explicit allowlists must contain `read_file`, while unsupported `delete` and `execute` are removed at model-request time.

Filesystem permissions are enforced by tool implementations with first-match path rules for ordinary operations and requested/resolved symlink targets; graph assembly turns interrupt rules into scope-aware HITL predicates, while bulk results filter only denied paths and a delete that may be recursive fails closed for any overlapping deny-write pattern.

Filesystem permission rules do not constrain shell command syntax: configuration with an execution-capable backend is rejected unless every rule is scoped to a `CompositeBackend` route, while `LocalShellBackend` executes commands directly on the host with the current user's permissions and no isolation.

`execute` is available only through `SandboxBackendProtocol` (or a composite default that implements it), validates a caller timeout against middleware and backend support, and returns a successful tool message with an exit-code artifact even when the command itself exits nonzero.
`BackendProtocol` makes `delete` optional and recursive, while `grep` and `glob` provide structured results that can be truncated; callers must not read a partial success as a complete search result.

The filesystem `grep` tool defaults to a total 1,000-match cap that callers can override or disable, and async protocol wrapping enforces a requested cap even for older backends that do not accept `max_count`.

`FilesystemBackend` defaults to `virtual_mode=True`, maps virtual absolute paths below `root_dir`, rejects traversal and resolved paths outside that root, and renders paths without leaking the host root; disabling virtual mode permits unrestricted host-path semantics.

FilesystemBackend's local `glob` applies shared basename-relative and dotfile-aware pattern semantics, rejects refused patterns as result errors, and returns partial matches marked with `truncation_reason="budget"` when its bounded walk expires.

FilesystemBackend batch upload and download preserve input order and report per-path errors, so a batch can partially succeed while traversal and common filesystem failures are standardized rather than escaping the backend boundary.

When execution is active on a CompositeBackend, FilesystemMiddleware supplies virtual-to-host route guidance only for FilesystemBackend routes sharing a LocalShellBackend default; it does not rewrite commands, and routes without that shared host filesystem remain file-tool-only.
